R6J-bear-backcountry-0002.name: 1.1 km E of Kwanika Creek
R6J-bear-backcountry-0002.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R6J-bear-backcountry-0002.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2021 (5 years old), right here: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
W facing slope, 10 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland 50 m W: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Village of Granisle, about 109 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 55.518, -125.33659, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 5.3 km SE, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 90 m, about 115 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 140 m NE of the spot at 1,016 m (55.4766, -125.2968). Water: unnamed wetland 190 m SW (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 7-28, Region 7A. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-01, closures 2026-10-16.
